review: A fun Metroidvania twin-stick platformer. Has its moments of jank, and some of the items are pretty blatant padding of the "if you come back here later, you can break this panel and get the item behind it" variety. But the movement is good, the level design is solid, and the writing is goofy fun.

Un juegazo del género "metroidvania" que viene de la era del poderoso Xbox 360 con un toque "moderno" en el sentido de que, tu personaje usa armamento, combate cuerpo a cuerpo y tecnología para moverse dentro de una base militar encontrada por "casualidad".

Tiene una historia que se quiere tomar muy en serio y ser muy oscura, pero me pareció cuando menos entretenida. 

Sin embargo su jugabilidad es algo de verdad maravilloso. Cuenta con controles bastante precisos y haces uso de ambos Sticks o palancas para moverte y apuntar tus armas. Sus gráficos en ese entonces me parecieron potentes, y creo que actualmente se pueden considerar decentes. 

El mundo es enorme y cuenta con una cantidad de secretos y power-ups bastante generosa. Tu personaje puede subir de nivel para hacer el viaje mas sencillo. Ver como se va volviendo cada vez mas rápido, resistente y con un armamento tan variado es la respuesta a la pregunta "¿Qué es lo que mas me gusta de los Metroidvania?".

Si quieres completar el juego al 100%, es decir, obtener todos los secretos y extras, prepárate ya que es un gran viaje. Los jefes son poderosos y algunos muy imponentes, pero tu, eres la verdadera amenaza.

9/10.

After hearing so many people call Shadow complex one of the best 'older' metroidvania's lost to time, I just had to try it out myself as i would consider myself a big fan of the genre. I've played over 70 MV's by now, featuring all the best like Ori, Blasphemous and FIST but also many atrocious ones like monster boy, dark light and 3000th duel. Opinions on what's the most important thing in an MV differ. Some people especially those who like soulslikes, would argue that combat is the most important but in my opinion level design and movement come first. Shadow complex nailed the former whilst fumblind the later. Level design is honestly great and makes the game feel like a proper MV, unfortunately movement veers on the clunkier side especially in regards to wall jumping. I cannot really give an informed opinion on combat as i played it on a lower difficulty which trivialized most bosses and encounters.

What i can say though is that the enemy AI is comically inadequette. They don't see your flashlight even in the dark only reacting if they see your body or hear you shoot. They really do feel like the dumb goons and grunts that serve the generic evil guy. Needless to say story isn't really the big focus here because it really feels like a 2000's game in that regard. That's not necesarilly bad though, i liked the cutscenes and animations as they gave me some sweet nostalgia to my playstation 2 back in the day. However it is hard to really care about the plot when it is so generic. The reason i played through the full game to 100% map completion is because the level design was just that good. However in the late game i really did feel the lack of fast travel when i had to run around picking up the final collectibles. Said collectibles are usefull initially when you gather the first few but later on what good is 2 more grenades when you already have 40+?

There's some other collectibles though that do feel more rewarding as well as one that eventually unlocks an immersion breaking cosmetic item that makes no sense but again reminds me of the sweet 2000's era of gaming. Unfortunately this time period was also know for the clunky animations which like i said were charming in cutscenes but in the gameplay they feel a bit spasmic. This further accentuated the poor controls as your character jumps around like he's having a seizure during platforming. The melee animations on the other hand were well done and often followed by hilarious ragdolling of enemies. The whole game is rather silly in its premise and execution so playing it like rambo feels adequette and entertaining. Which is why i'm glad i went with a lower difficulty because it allowed me to blast through mech bosses and literal armies at the end.

Visuals then hold up well enough in terms of texture quality thanks to the remaster. And given how many different background elements they are, assets are also of considerable quality. I was actually quite amazed how little copy pasting there was in terms of environments, which is rare for an MV. The 2.5D looked pretty good given it's age but the closest comparison, FIST forged in shadow torch, had more charm to it. Maybe the more grounded setting taking place on actual earth was what made it lose some charm as i prefer fictional worlds. Still though the place does feel like an underground complex and little details add some character. However the generic soundtrack does little to elevate the atmosphere beyond that. At least your immersion won't get broken due to framerate issues or crashes although some bugs can be encountered. It's a decent enough game that sits in the upper middle of the MV tier list.

Waited seven years for this to come out on PC and for twenty bucks it's pretty good.  Got a bit of the Super Metroid heavier movement to it, and the 3D in a 2D game aiming takes a little getting used to, but once you get past that you got a nice diversion.

Shadow Complex is not a perfect game. The wall jumping can be unreliable. You can make the (normal version of the) best gun in the game unobtainable if you pass a point of no return too early. Two of the collectible items are harder to get because they are placed in save rooms, meaning they don't show up on the map. Instant death rooms and lasers are a pain. The plot of the game and the books it ties into has aged horribly, especially after 2020.

Despite those complaints, this is still a game I can't help but like. In a genre that is ususally focused on science fiction or fantasy, Shadow Complex's focus on military action makes it unique. You aren't slaying monsters in a castle, or blasting aliens in outer space, you're just a schlub in over his head, sneaking around a military base. Like Die Hard, if it took place in a Cobra or Hydra base. The utilization of the 2.5D design of the game to shoot enemies in the background mostly works and I haven't seen many, or any other games in the genre attempt it. The character growth from being a nobody with a pea shooter to a super soldier is satisfying. It feels good to stomp on enemies that would've been serious challenges earlier on.

Calling it one of the best search action, metroidvania games might be a little much, but I think it'll be a good time for fans of the genre who want something a little different.

You know, as long as you're willing to put up with Orson Scott Card's silly ideas.
